name: SNAP-8

lead: SNAP-8 (acetyl octapeptide-3) is a longer analogue of Argireline marketed for reducing expression wrinkles. It appears in anti-aging serums and eye creams.
Publicly available evidence is limited and mostly from manufacturers; independent controlled trials are scarce.

paras: Like Argireline, it is designed to imitate part of SNAP-25 and interfere with SNARE complex assembly to lower neurotransmitter release at the muscle junction, though skin delivery is reported to limit its effect.
It is considered low risk and is unrestricted as a cosmetic ingredient. Reported effects are modest and reversible.

lead: SNAP-8, the trade name of acetyl octapeptide-3, is a synthetic peptide used as a topical cosmetic ingredient in serums and eye products marketed for expression lines, particularly on the forehead and around the eyes [1]. It is described as an extended analogue of acetyl hexapeptide-8 (Argireline), built on the same SNAP-25-derived sequence with additional amino acids at one end [1][2].

Like Argireline, it is proposed to compete with the protein SNAP-25 in assembling the SNARE complex, which would reduce neurotransmitter release at the neuromuscular junction and so muscle contraction, in a manner conceptually similar to botulinum toxin but milder and reversible [1][2].

Published evidence specific to SNAP-8 is sparse. A 2020 review reported no peer-reviewed clinical study of the peptide on its own and noted that the wrinkle-reduction figures in circulation come from the manufacturer's website; the human studies that exist test it as one ingredient among several [2][3][4].
infobox: Acetyl octapeptide-3 (also listed as acetyl glutamyl heptapeptide-1) [1]
Cosmetic ingredient; not an approved drug

paras: SNAP-8 is a linear peptide with an acetylated N-terminus and amidated C-terminus. Its sequence contains that of Argireline plus an alanine-aspartate extension [1][2]. Descriptions in the literature use inconsistent names for it, including octapeptide and heptapeptide labels [2].

Proponents and manufacturers describe it as a competitive inhibitor of SNARE complex formation. A 2020 review reported that in an in vitro assay a 1.5 millimolar concentration inhibited release by about 43 percent, and that combining SNAP-8 with another peptide gave a larger effect than either alone in that assay [2]. Grokipedia states that manufacturer data indicated greater wrinkle reduction than for Argireline in a 17-woman test, while noting that independent clinical evidence is limited [1].

A 2024 comparative study in 24 adults aged 30 to 65 (21 completed) tested a dissolving hyaluronic acid microneedle eye patch that contained SNAP-8 (0.03 percent) together with ascorbic acid glucoside and sodium cyclic lysophosphatidic acid, against a hyaluronic acid-only patch, applied to each eye of the same person. Several skin-roughness measures improved versus placebo by day 28, and the authors reported no erythema, oedema or scaling. The authors attribute early effects to SNAP-8 and later effects mainly to the other ingredients; the study was small, did not clearly state blinding, and several authors were employees of the patch manufacturer [3].

A 2020 single-centre clinical study examined hyaluronic acid microneedle patches loaded with several bioactive peptides for dermal tolerability and anti-ageing effect; as a multi-ingredient product, its results cannot be assigned to one peptide [4]. No published randomised trial has tested SNAP-8 alone against placebo or against botulinum toxin, according to the 2020 review of cosmeceutical peptides [2].

No adverse events beyond normal skin tolerance were reported in the small microneedle patch study [3]. Grokipedia describes the ingredient as having shallower skin penetration and lower potency than injected botulinum toxin and as free of the injection-related risks of that procedure [1]. No long-term or pregnancy safety data specific to SNAP-8 were identified.

SNAP-8 appears as a named ingredient in anti-ageing serums and eye creams, usually at very low final concentrations, and is often marketed alongside or as an upgrade to Argireline [1]. Wikipedia has no article on the compound (a search for "SNAP-8" returns an unrelated nuclear power programme), and no substantial discussion of it in looksmaxxing forums was found.
